question.prompt: It takes \(5\) seconds for a clock to strike \(6\) o’clock beginning at \(6{:}00\) o’clock precisely. If the strikings are uniformly spaced, how long, in seconds, does it take to strike \(12\) o’clock?

solutions.explanation:
The first strike occurs precisely at the starting time, so the elapsed time comes from the gaps between strikes. Six strikes have \(6-1=5\) gaps. Since these equal gaps take \(5\) seconds altogether, each gap lasts \(5\div5=1\) second.

Twelve strikes have \(12-1=11\) gaps, so they take \(11\cdot1=11\) seconds. The answer is \(\boxed{11}\), choice C.
solutions.title: Count the gaps
